passage:
Dear Ujjwal Mama,

I'm writing because I don't know how to say this on the phone. Since the separation, Mummy sleeps very late and often forgets things. Last Tuesday there was no dinner, and I had cereal. She forgot to sign my exam form, and the last date is Friday. I'm not blaming her. I think she's sad and tired, and it isn't because of me.

Could you help me with the exam form on Wednesday? And could I have dinner at your house two evenings a week for now? I'll get myself there after school.

I'd also like someone to ask how I'm doing. Sometimes I feel forgotten.

Thank you,
Parveen

Mama's reply, that same evening: "Thank you for telling me. None of this is your fault. I'm coming over tomorrow, and we'll do the form together."

qa.q: Which day is the last date for the exam form?
What is Parveen feeling about Mummy's forgetfulness?
qa.a: Parveen feels hurt and sometimes forgotten, yet does not blame Mummy and thinks she is sad and tired.

qa.q: What is Parveen doing that could help meet Parveen's needs?
qa.a: Parveen is asking clearly for help with the form, regular dinners and someone to check in, and is turning to a relative.

qa.q: How might Ujjwal Mama feel reading the letter?
qa.a: Probably worried and touched that Parveen trusted him, and eager to help Parveen and check on his sister as well; he replies that same evening.

grounding: Shows a teen whose parent is absorbed in pain and forgets meals and exam forms, asking a relative clearly for what they need.

passage:
Dear Sahil Mama,
I hope you're well in Kochi. I'm writing because Mummy says you're the one she listens to.
Since Papa left, Mummy mostly stays in her room. Some nights there's no dinner, and I make instant noodles for myself. Last week she forgot my science practical exam and I nearly missed it. I know she's hurting. I don't think she's stopped loving me. She just can't see much right now.
On Sunday I told her clearly, "Mummy, I need dinner on school nights and I need you to know my exam dates." She cried and said sorry.
Today my class teacher, Mrs Kapoor, saw me skip lunch. She shared her tiffin, and she phoned Mummy this afternoon to talk about how to help.
Could you come for a few days, or call Mummy more often? I'd feel less alone.
Rekha

qa.q: Which exam did Mummy forget last week?
How is Rekha feeling about Mummy's forgetting?
qa.a: Rekha feels lonely and hurt but also understanding, believing Mummy is in pain rather than unloving.

qa.q: What wise steps has Rekha taken?
qa.a: Rekha asked Mummy clearly for dinner and exam support, accepted help from Mrs Kapoor, and is reaching out to Sahil Mama for more support.

qa.q: How might Mrs Kapoor see what happened at lunch?
qa.a: The teacher seems concerned when Rekha skips lunch, so shares a tiffin and phones Mummy the same day to work out how to help.

grounding: A teen whose parent is lost in her own pain asks clearly for what is needed and turns to a teacher and an uncle.

passage:
So you asked how I got through Class 12. Honestly? Barely. I'm Hemant, by the way, for anyone just tuning in.
When my parents split, Papa got custody for the school year. He was in his own fog. He forgot parent-teacher day. He forgot I'd told him my board dates. Once I came home from a chemistry paper and there was nothing to eat, not even bread.
For a while I thought, maybe I'm just not worth remembering. That was the worst part.
Then one night I wrote my exam dates on a big sheet and taped it to the fridge. I told him, "Papa, I need you to see this every day." He looked at it for a long time and said, "I've been failing you, son, haven't I."
And I started going to my Dadi's flat, two streets away, for dinner. She'd ask about every paper.
That's how. One sheet on the fridge, and one grandmother.

qa.q: Where did Hemant tape the exam dates?
How did Hemant feel when Papa kept forgetting things?
qa.a: Hemant felt hurt and unimportant, even wondering whether he was worth remembering at all.

qa.q: What helped Hemant most, and why?
qa.a: Asking Papa clearly with the sheet on the fridge, and leaning on Dadi for dinners and interest in his papers, gave him both attention and care.

qa.q: How does Papa seem to feel when he sees the sheet on the fridge?
qa.a: He seems shaken and regretful, realising for the first time how much he has neglected his son during his own pain.

grounding: A teen whose father forgot his meals and exams during the divorce asks clearly for what he needs and leans on his grandmother.
